description: Replace each {$array: i} with arrays[i]; all values are precomputed.

methods.title: Raw RMSE
methods.keeps: This view keeps absolute level, amplitude and timestamp identity.
methods.allows: It allows no time shift or local realignment.
methods.caution: A vertical offset is a real difference under this rule, even when both shapes look alike.
methods.contribution: Squared residual / n; bars sum to RMSE²

methods.title: z-normalized RMSE
methods.preprocess: Separate mean removal and population-SD scaling for A and B.
methods.keeps: This view keeps fluctuations at the same timestamps after standardization.
methods.allows: It allows an additive offset and a positive gain to disappear.
methods.caution: It still penalizes phase or timing changes. Constant sequences are excluded from this lab.
methods.contribution: Squared standardized residual / n; sum = z-RMSE²

methods.title: Pearson correlation
methods.preprocess: Separate mean removal and population-SD scaling for A and B.
methods.keeps: This view keeps same-time linear co-fluctuation and its sign.
methods.allows: It allows offset and positive gain; a negative gain reverses the sign.
methods.caution: Correlation is not amplitude agreement. Here z-RMSE² = 2(1-r), up to rounding.
methods.parameters: No lag search; no significance test
methods.contribution: Signed product / n; bars sum to r

methods.title: SBD / best linear lag NCC
methods.preprocess: Per-series z-score, then zero-padded linear cross-correlation.
methods.keeps: This view keeps standardized waveform agreement under one global lag.
methods.allows: It allows a single shift, offset and positive gain; it cannot locally stretch time.
methods.caution: This is not circular correlation. Plot gaps are zero-padded terms; lost support can reduce the score. Full-series energies remain in the denominator.
methods.contribution: NCC at every linear lag; gold line marks the chosen lag

methods.title: DTW with an eight-sample band
methods.keeps: This view keeps amplitude and chronological order, including both endpoints.
methods.allows: It allows repeated matches and local timing changes inside a fixed band.
methods.caution: It returns sqrt(total squared path cost), not RMSE or a path-length-normalized score. The band can prevent a desired match.
methods.contribution: Squared costs grouped by A index; sum = DTW²

methods.title: First-difference RMSE
methods.preprocess: First differences of raw amplitudes; sampling interval=1.
methods.keeps: This view keeps local upward and downward increments at the same intervals.
methods.allows: It allows a constant vertical offset to disappear; positive gain still matters.
methods.caution: This is a chosen derivative comparison, not derivative-DTW. Noise and narrow events can produce large differences.

methods.title: Fourier-magnitude distance
methods.preprocess: Raw input; orthonormal rFFT; keep magnitudes including DC.
methods.keeps: This view keeps the strength of every non-negative frequency, including the mean.
methods.allows: It allows phase changes, circular shifts and exact reversal to have identical features.
methods.caution: The 33 unique bins are unweighted; interior bins are not multiplied by sqrt(2). This is not waveform Euclidean distance or physical PSD.
methods.contribution: Squared magnitude gaps; sum = magnitude L2²

sources.title: NumPy: real DFT and Hermitian symmetry

methods.title: Autocorrelation-profile distance
methods.preprocess: Remove each mean; divide lag products by (n-lag) × population variance.
methods.keeps: This view keeps within-series recurrence at lags 1 through 12.
methods.allows: It allows offset, nonzero gain and exact reversal to share the same ACF.
methods.caution: This is finite-window adjusted ACF, not circular ACF. Circular shifts or arbitrary phase changes need not leave it fixed; adjusted values may exceed ±1.
methods.contribution: Squared ACF gaps; sum = ACF L2²

methods.title: PAA block-mean distance
methods.preprocess: Raw input; average eight disjoint blocks of eight samples.
methods.keeps: This view keeps the coarse amplitude profile and the order of its blocks.
methods.allows: It allows within-block fluctuations to disappear when their averages agree.
methods.caution: The score is an unscaled feature L2. It does not include the sqrt(n/blocks) factor used for the usual Euclidean lower bound.
methods.contribution: Squared block-mean gaps; sum = feature L2²

methods.title: SAX MINDIST lower bound
methods.preprocess: Per-series z-score → eight PAA means → four Gaussian-quantile symbols.
methods.keeps: This view keeps ordered coarse levels after standardization and quantization.
methods.allows: It allows offset, positive gain and some nearby symbolic levels to share a zero lower bound.
methods.caution: Zero MINDIST does not prove equal waveforms or even equal symbols: adjacent symbol intervals have zero minimum separation.
methods.contribution: Eight × squared interval gaps; sum = MINDIST²

sources.title: Lin et al. (2007): SAX and MINDIST

methods.title: LCSS tolerance matches
methods.keeps: This view keeps the longest ordered set of one-to-one tolerance matches.
methods.allows: It allows skips and timing differences within eight samples; unmatched points carry no squared-error penalty.
methods.caution: The score depends on epsilon in raw amplitude units. A high matched fraction can hide a local event that was skipped.
methods.contribution: Matched A positions (1) and skipped positions (0)

perturbations.title: Vertical offset
perturbations.description: B = A + 1.5s. Every timestamp keeps its original position.
perturbations.observe: Compare raw RMSE with z-RMSE: removing each series' mean removes this offset.

perturbations.title: Positive gain
perturbations.description: B = (1 + 1.4s) A. The multiplier stays positive; there is no clipping.
perturbations.observe: Pearson and z-RMSE discard positive amplitude scaling; raw amplitude methods retain it.

perturbations.title: Circular global shift
perturbations.description: B = roll(A, level), for integer levels 0 to 20. Samples wrap at the boundary.
perturbations.observe: DFT magnitudes are unchanged by a circular shift. SBD searches zero-padded linear lags, so boundary loss can remain.

perturbations.title: Local time warp
perturbations.description: B[i] = interp(A, i + 6s sin²(pi i/63)). The sampling map is increasing and fixes both endpoints.
perturbations.observe: DTW can change local correspondences within its eight-sample band. Interpolation can still leave residual error.

perturbations.title: Local pulse / event
perturbations.description: B[i] = A[i] + 3s exp(-0.5((i-44)/1.2)²). Only a short region changes appreciably.
perturbations.observe: Pointwise costs locate the event. LCSS can leave it unmatched, depending on its amplitude tolerance.

perturbations.title: Fourier phase change
perturbations.description: Rotate interior rFFT bins by s*pi*sin(0.83k). Keep the original real DC and Nyquist coefficients; invert with irFFT.
perturbations.observe: All rFFT magnitudes stay fixed while the waveform changes. Finite-window ACF need not stay fixed.

perturbations.title: Blend toward time reversal
perturbations.description: B = (1-s)A + s reverse(A). At s=1 the order is exactly reversed; intermediate mixtures need not preserve the spectrum.
perturbations.observe: At full reversal, DFT magnitudes and finite-window ACF coincide. Pointwise and order-preserving alignments can still differ.
